task.description: Idiom/scope gate on REQ-243 (queue task 481, ISS-0424 part 3b-1): applying REQ-237's .zig provenance-marking convention to lib/letflow/router.ex and lib/letflow/routers/{audit,definitions,dlq,identity,instances,metrics_exposition,onboarding}.ex. Branch feature/WF02-REQ243-20260905, commit 8c48f359, off main@8a62f9cc.

result.summary: Independently re-verified all of ELIXIR-DEV's claims by direct grep/diff against main and the branch, not by trusting the handoff. Findings: (1) Pre-existing marker count is 0 in all 8 files on main; post-change counts (3/7/13/1/6/5/1/2, total 38) match exactly. (2) .zig line count is identical before/after in all 8 files (14/7/15/1/11/5/1/2). (3) An awk scan for any .zig line not preceded by a marker within the same blank-line-delimited block found zero residuals in all 8 files -- no citation escaped marking. (4) git diff --stat confirms only the 8 in-scope files plus the two handoff JSONs changed; the full diff shows every hunk is a pure `+PROVENANCE (historical, not current decision authority):` line insertion, no citation path text touched. (5) metrics_exposition.ex's 'unlike R-Co' staleness line: diffed main:line67 against branch:line68 directly -- byte-identical, confirmed shifted by exactly one line from the single marker inserted earlier in the same moduledoc. (6) definitions.ex heading+bullets: read the actual section -- the heading '## Two different R-Co files are called validation.zig...' is itself a self-contained line carrying a .zig substring (structurally the same as design section 2's 'lone bullet like phrasing 4' single-citation-line case), and the two list bullets beneath it are each their own 'lone bullet' single-citation-line unit per section 2's explicit definition (unit continues only across hard-wrapped continuation lines of the same bullet, not across sibling bullets) -- marking all three separately is the CORRECT reading of the design, not scope creep or a merge error.

flagged_judgment_call_resolved.question: Do the 6 markers inserted inside plain Elixir `#` comment blocks (audit.ex x1, definitions.ex x3, identity.ex x1, instances.ex x1), prefixed '# ' to keep valid Elixir syntax, break the design's single-regex greppability property (AC-2)?
flagged_judgment_call_resolved.verdict: No design gap -- ELIXIR-DEV's adaptation is correct and does not need rework. Tested directly: `grep -c`, `grep -Ec`, and `grep -Fc` against the literal marker text ('PROVENANCE (historical, not current decision authority):') all match a '# '-prefixed line exactly the same as a bare line (count 1 in both /tmp test files) -- the design's own verification command in section 5 (`grep -rc 'PROVENANCE (historical, not current decision authority):' lib/ docs/`) is a plain substring match with no line-start anchor, so it finds the marker regardless of a leading '# '. This is not the same situation the design rejected in section 2's trade-off discussion -- that alternative was styling the marker DIFFERENTLY per directory (HTML-comment form in docs/, '#'-comment form in lib/) requiring an OR-branch to find both forms. Here the literal marker text is identical everywhere; the '# ' prefix is a minimal syntactic necessity for a context (bare Elixir source comments outside any heredoc/string) the design doc's section 2 genuinely never enumerates (it only discusses moduledoc-heredoc and Markdown contexts, both of which tolerate the bare unstyled line as valid prose/string content). Zero regex changes needed; a single grep still finds every marker in every context. Worth a documentation follow-up (amend req237's design doc section 2 or 3 to explicitly enumerate the bare-# -comment context and its '# ' prefix so future chunks -- e.g. any of REQ-244..253 that hit a bare code comment -- don't have to re-derive this same judgment call from scratch), but that is a design-doc completeness note, not a rework blocker on this diff.

result.idiom_scope_supervision_check: N/A to this requirement's own content -- this is a pure documentation/comment text-insertion change (Markdown/moduledoc/comment lines only), touching zero process/supervision/state-machine code. No gen_statem, GenServer, InstanceSupervisor, or type/struct code is touched by this diff, so review questions 1-3 (idiom vs crutch, supervision, type-safety gaps) do not apply -- confirmed by reading the full diff end to end, which contains only `+` marker-line insertions and zero logic changes.
result.scope_creep_check: None. The 38 markers inserted are exactly what REQ-237's design mandates applied mechanically to this chunk's 8 files; no additional abstraction, behaviour, or plumbing was introduced. Files touched match REQ-243's scope exactly (verified via git diff --stat); no sibling-chunk file (e.g. promotions.ex) was touched.
result.test_designer_routing: SKIP is correct. This is pure text insertion with no logic/behavior change -- confirmed by ORCH's own independently-verified mix compile --warnings-as-errors (clean), mix format --check-formatted (clean), and mix test across router_test.exs + 9 routers test files (258 passed, 0 failures), plus my own confirmation that the diff contains no non-comment/non-moduledoc changes. No new test coverage is needed for a documentation-only change; existing test suite already demonstrates zero behavioral regression.
